_help: Festival & wedding-season engine. One list of dated events for the next 12+ months. The build uses it for: homepage banners (India visitors: from lead.india_start days before until the day before; visitors abroad: from lead.intl_start until lead.intl_stop days before), festival shop pages (events with a 'page'), feed custom labels, and the 'last order date' table. scripts/festival-engine.mjs writes social/email drafts to drafts/ when an event's lead time starts. audience: india = banner for India visitors only, intl = visitors abroad only, both = both. theme = the banner theme id in content/banners/calendar/banner-calendar.json (no theme = no banner). Dates: only verified dates; 'note' says when calendars differ by a day. Extend every month (weekly routine checks covers_until).

christmas-new-year.h1: Indian Outfits for Christmas & New Year's Eve
christmas-new-year.title: Indian Christmas & New Year Outfits for Women {year}
christmas-new-year.description: Velvet Anarkalis, red & green suits and black-and-gold party sets for Christmas and New Year's Eve – with the last order dates for the USA, UK, Canada, UAE, Australia and India.
christmas-new-year.intro: Red, green, wine and velvet for Christmas – black, gold and jewel tones for New Year's Eve. Stitched in Jaipur, shipped with duties paid.

guide.heading: How to wear Indian outfits for Christmas and New Year

p: For a church service or family lunch, pick a kurta set or an Anarkali with sleeves and a dupatta – it is warm, covered and easy to sit in for a long meal. Deep red, bottle green, wine and ivory with gold all feel festive without looking bridal.
For a Christmas party, velvet is the easiest choice in winter: it holds colour beautifully under warm lights and keeps you warm between the car and the door.

sections.h: New Year's Eve: party looks with an Indian touch
p: Black, navy, wine and emerald with gold lace or gota work photograph well at night. A flared Anarkali moves well on the dance floor; a straight suit with a statement dupatta is easier if you will be standing for hours.

list: Wear thermal leggings under straight pants or palazzos.
Carry a long coat or a velvet or pashmina shawl over the dupatta.
Choose ankle boots or closed juttis for cold or wet streets.

faq: Can I wear an Indian outfit to a Christmas party?
Yes. A velvet Anarkali or an embroidered suit in red, green or wine fits Christmas parties well, in India and abroad. Choose a lighter dupatta if the party is crowded.
What colours are best for New Year's Eve?
Black, gold, navy, wine and emerald are the classic party colours. Add shine with lace, gota or zari borders rather than a heavy dupatta.
When should I order for delivery before Christmas?
Use the last order dates on this page. They include our dispatch time and the slowest delivery time, so order a few days earlier if you can.

lohri.title: Lohri Outfits for Women {year}: Suits & Kurta Sets
lohri.description: Bright Punjabi suits, kurta sets and Anarkalis for Lohri – mustard, red and rani pink with warm layers for the bonfire. Last order dates for India, USA, UK and Canada.
lohri.intro: Bright, happy colours for the bonfire night – with room for a warm shawl. Stitched to your size in Jaipur.

guide.heading: What to wear for Lohri

p: Lohri is a Punjabi harvest festival celebrated around a bonfire on the night before Makar Sankranti. Bright colours suit it best: mustard, red, rani pink, orange and phulkari-style brights. Darker greens and wine also look rich in the firelight.

list: Choose cotton, cotton-blend or velvet rather than very sheer synthetics near the bonfire.
Keep the dupatta pinned or draped over one shoulder so it stays away from the fire.
Straight pants or palazzos are easier than very long flares when you walk around the fire and do the bhangra.

p: In the UK, Canada and the USA, Lohri is often held indoors or in a community hall in January cold. Layer a velvet suit or a long jacket and keep a warm shawl for the outdoor bonfire.

faq: What colour should I wear for Lohri?
Bright colours – mustard, red, rani pink and orange – are the traditional Lohri colours. Deep green and wine look good too.
What should a new bride wear for her first Lohri?
Many brides wear a red or rani pink suit or Anarkali with gota or embroidery, and their wedding chooda. Keep the dupatta well away from the fire.
Yes – velvet is warm and rich for a January night, especially in the UK, Canada or North India.

pongal-makar-sankranti.title: Pongal & Makar Sankranti Outfits for Women {year}
pongal-makar-sankranti.description: Yellow, green and festive cotton kurta sets and Anarkalis for Pongal, Makar Sankranti and Uttarayan – plus last order dates for India and abroad.
pongal-makar-sankranti.intro: Sunny yellows, fresh greens and comfortable festive cottons for the Pongal pot, kite flying and family lunches.

guide.heading: What to wear for Pongal and Makar Sankranti

p: Makar Sankranti marks the sun's move into Capricorn. It is Pongal in Tamil Nadu, Uttarayan in Gujarat, Magh Bihu in Assam and Sankranti in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka. The colours change a little by region, but bright, sunny and festive is right everywhere.

list: Pongal: yellow, green, orange and white with gold – traditionally silk sarees or pavadai, but a festive kurta set with a zari border fits a temple visit or family lunch.
Uttarayan: bright cottons you can spend the whole day on the terrace in – kites, sun and dust.
Choose breathable cotton or chanderi in South India; add a shawl or a velvet layer in North India and abroad.

faq: What colour is worn on Makar Sankranti?
Yellow, orange and green are the most common festive colours. In Maharashtra many women wear black on Sankranti, as it is a winter festival.
Can I wear a kurta set for Pongal?
Yes. Many women wear silk sarees, but a kurta set or Anarkali in yellow, green or white with gold is a comfortable choice for a temple visit or a family lunch.
Is Makar Sankranti on 14 or 15 January 2027?

In 2027 the sun enters Makara on the night of 14 January (India time), so most Indian calendars observe Makar Sankranti and Pongal on Friday, 15 January. Some calendars and temples abroad list 14 January.
